title: Hanging Indent in Google Docs and Word | AnswerThis
summary: A hanging indent keeps the first line at the margin and indents the rest 0.5 inch. Follow the steps for Google Docs and Word, with APA and MLA examples.
body_markdown:
A hanging indent keeps the first line of a reference at the left margin and indents every line after it, usually by 0.5 inch. APA and MLA both ask for it in the reference list.


This guide gives the steps for Google Docs and for Word on Windows and Mac. It then shows what APA, MLA and Chicago ask for, and how to fix a hanging indent that will not work.


## TL;DR


-


Google Docs: Format, Align & indent, Indentation options, then set Special indent to Hanging.


-


Word on Windows: Home, Paragraph Settings, then set Special to Hanging.


-


Word on Mac: Format, Paragraph, then set Special to Hanging.


-


APA and MLA both use a 0.5 inch hanging indent.


## What is a hanging indent?


A hanging indent is a paragraph format. The first line starts at the left margin. The second line and every line after it start 0.5 inch to the right.


It is used in reference lists because it makes each entry easy to find. The first word of every entry, usually the author's last name, stands out at the margin.


## How do you do a hanging indent in Google Docs?


### Use the Indentation options menu


1.


Select the reference entries you want to format.


2.


Click Format in the top menu.


3.


Point to Align & indent, then click Indentation options.


4.


Under Special indent, choose Hanging. The box beside it shows 0.5 by default. Keep it.


5.


Click Apply.


### Use the ruler


You can also set the indent on the ruler above the page. If you cannot see the ruler, click View, then Show ruler.


1.


Select the reference entries.


2.


Drag the small triangle on the ruler to the 0.5 inch mark. This is the Left indent marker. The whole entry moves to the right.


3.


Drag the small rectangle above the triangle back to the left margin. This is the First line indent marker. Only the first line moves back.


The menu method is easier to get exactly right, so use it if the ruler markers are hard to grab.


## How do you do a hanging indent in Word?


Use the following[steps](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/word/create-a-hanging-indent-in-word#tabpanel_2_macos) .


### Word on Windows


1.


Select the reference entries you want to format.


2.


On the Home tab, click the small arrow in the corner of the Paragraph group. This opens Paragraph Settings.


3.


On the Indents and Spacing tab, find Special and choose Hanging.


4.


Keep the By box at 0.5 inch, then select OK.


### Word on Mac


1.


Select the reference entries.


2.


Click Format in the menu bar, then Paragraph.


3.


Under Special, choose Hanging.


4.


Keep the By box at 0.5 inch, then select OK.


### The keyboard shortcut


Select the entries and press Ctrl+T on Windows or Command+T on a Mac. Word applies a hanging indent straight away.


## What do APA, MLA and Chicago ask for?


All three styles use a hanging indent in the list of sources. The examples below show one entry in each style. In your document, any line after the first would be indented 0.5 inch.


### APA 7


[APA](https://apastyle.apa.org/style-grammar-guidelines/paper-format/reference-list) asks for a 0.5 inch hanging indent on the whole reference list. The list is also double-spaced.


American Psychological Association. (2020). *Publication manual of the American Psychological Association* (7th ed.). https://doi.org/10.1037/0000165-000


### MLA 9


[MLA](https://owl.purdue.edu/owl/research_and_citation/mla_style/mla_formatting_and_style_guide/mla_works_cited_page_basic_format.html) asks you to indent the second and later lines of each works-cited entry by 0.5 inch.


*MLA Handbook* . 9th ed., Modern Language Association of America, 2021.


### Chicago


[Chicago](https://libguides.up.edu/chicago) style bibliographies also use a hanging indent by 0.5 inch.


*The Chicago Manual of Style* . 17th ed. Chicago: University of Chicago Press, 2017.


If you are not sure which style your paper needs, our[APA vs MLA](https://answerthis.io/blog/apa-vs-mla) guide compares the two.


## How do you fix a hanging indent that will not work?


If the indent looks wrong after you apply it, one of these four problems is usually the cause.


-


The citation was pasted with its old formatting. Paste it again as plain text, then apply the hanging indent.


-


The entry has manual line breaks. If someone pressed Enter at the end of each line, every line is a separate paragraph. Delete the breaks so the entry is one paragraph.


-


The indent was made with tabs or spaces. Delete them, then apply the hanging indent from the menu.


-


The entries are in a bulleted or numbered list. Turn the list formatting off first.


If the whole entry moves to the right, you set a left indent and not a hanging indent. Open the same menu, set the left indent to 0 and choose Hanging under Special.


## Get the citation right before you indent it


The indent only fixes the layout. The citation itself still has to follow the style. The AnswerThis[MLA citation generator](https://answerthis.io/mla-citation-generator) creates MLA 9 citations from source details, and the AnswerThis[APA citation generator](https://answerthis.io/apa-citation-generator) does the same for APA 7. Your first 3 sources are free. Paste the citation into your document, then apply the hanging indent with the steps above.


## FAQs


### How big should a hanging indent be?


Use 0.5 inch, which is 1.27 cm. APA and MLA both ask for this size.


### What is the hanging indent shortcut in Word?


Press Ctrl+T on Windows or Command+T on a Mac after you select the entries.


### Do APA and MLA both need a hanging indent?


Yes. APA uses it for the reference list and MLA uses it for the works-cited list.


### How do I remove a hanging indent?


Open the same menu you used to add it. In Google Docs, set Special indent to None. In Word, set Special to None.


### Why does my pasted citation lose its indent?


The hanging indent is a setting in your document, not part of the citation text. Apply it after you paste.
